title: Onboarding PRD: Compatibility Declarations and Negotiated Version‑Lock Flow
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: PRD and acceptance checklist that defines how new open-model submissions must declare runtime compatibility, negotiate temporary version-lock agreements with Redwood runtime, and satisfy automated liveness/compatibility probes before the model is allowed into the catalog's routed surface. This doc clarifies scope changes from prior intake guidance and enumerates fallback behavior and rollback triggers.
scope_in_scope: Machine-readable compatibility declaration schema (.compat.json) that model contributors submit with weights
Negotiated version-lock workflow: temporary lock requests, TTL-based lock agreements, and rollback windows
Automated runtime probes (integration test harness) that run a canonical prompt suite across target hardware/quantization settings
Acceptance criteria for 'soft-admit' (limited traffic) vs 'full-admit' status
Operational signals required for catalog entry: perf profile, failure-mode doc, recommended fallback models
scope_out_of_scope: Model training quality assessments (we rely on submitter-provided evals)
Billing or pricing changes for admitted models
Native tooling for model quantization (we will reference recommendations only)
acceptance_criteria: Contributor supplies valid .compat.json that declares: supported sequence lengths, required kernel features, preferred quantization artifacts, and semantic version for weights
Runtime integration tests (CI) complete with: <90ms 95p-normalized latency delta vs baseline for supported sequences OR documented trade-offs accepted by PM
KV/prefix caching semantics validated for chat workloads; no uncontrolled token inflation observed on the canonical chat prompts
If version-lock is requested, submitter provides a lock TTL (max 90 days) and a migration plan; Redwood approves or counters within 5 business days
Soft-admit gate: model serves up to 1% of traffic with per-token cost and quality monitored for 7 days before full admit decision
Clear fallback mapping exists (catalog id -> fallback model id) for graceful degradation in case of runtime regressions
Security review completed for models claiming FHE/KMS integrations or handling regulated PII

decisions: Require machine-readable .compat.json on first submission — human summaries allowed but not substitute.
Adopt 90-day maximum for negotiated version-lock TTL; auto-escalation 30 days before expiry to requestor and runtime owners.
Soft-admit window set to 7 days by default with 1% traffic cap; can be extended by PM or runtime owners with justification.
Probe harness to run against a dedicated pre-admit sandbox to avoid slowing mainline CI; results must be recorded in catalog entry metadata.
tradeoffs: Strict machine-readable requirements reduce onboarding friction for runtime engineering but raise bar for community contributors; mitigated by providing templates and a lightweight CLI validator.
90-day version-lock TTL favors stability for customers but may block timely upstream fixes; TTL renewals will require a migration plan to reduce vendor stagnation.
Soft-admit reduces blast radius of regressions but increases time-to-full-availability for contributors; balanced with monitoring automation and rollback triggers.
